answer: A practical defence is to require each agent to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly and is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Spinning up thousands of fakes then stops being free: an attacker must fund every identity and risks losing all of it when one cluster is exposed. The cost can spiral because investigators follow shared funding trails and coordinated behaviour from a single summit of evidence back to the whole ring. Even a faint pigment-like fingerprint, repeated across accounts, betrays the group before any payout is released.
